use_case: Generative AI virtual assistant answering prospective students' program, cost, and admissions questions on the website and in the CRM chat
vendor_or_model: CRM vendor generative AI feature (vendor-hosted foundation model; no training on company data by contract)
data_categories: Inquiry questions; contact details; program interest (no aid or account data)
consequential_decision_category: None (answers questions; hands off to an enrollment advisor; no scoring)
human_in_the_loop: Escalates to an advisor on request, on aid or eligibility questions, and on any complaint; AI disclosure at the start of every chat
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 (accuracy of program and cost claims); Utah AI Policy Act disclosure (met by disclosure at the start); state consumer protection laws generally
bias_testing_status: Not applicable (no decisions about individuals); answer accuracy tested
monitoring: Monthly 200-transcript sample for accuracy and prohibited claims (job placement, earnings, aid guarantees)

use_case: Admissions inquiry and applicant scoring: ranks about 1.6 million inquiries a year and open applications by predicted likelihood to enroll; sorts enrollment advisors' call queues
vendor_or_model: CRM vendor predictive scoring feature (model trained on pooled data across the vendor's clients, then calibrated on the College's history)
data_categories: Inquiry source; program of interest; engagement (email opens, page visits); home ZIP code; age band; prior education; military affiliation; employer sponsorship; device type
consequential_decision_category: Education (who receives advisor contact and how fast)
human_in_the_loop: Advisors may call any inquiry; until 2026-08-26 inquiries scoring under 20 were routed to automated email only with no advisor call (now stopped)
applicable_laws: Title VI; Title IX; Section 504; Age Discrimination Act; FERPA once a student matriculates; FTC Safeguards Rule 16 CFR 314.4(f) (vendor); FTC Act Section 5; Colorado SB26-189 and California CPPA ADMT rules from 2027-01-01 (P03 G-079, G-080)
status: In production (enabled 2026-03-02 through CRM tenant configuration)
committee_review: Not reviewed before enablement; interim decision 2026-08-25 (section 9); full review due 2026-12-15 (POAM-019)
protected_characteristic_inputs: Age band; home ZIP code (proxy for race and income); device type (proxy for income)
bias_testing_status: Vendor-supplied tests on pooled data for sex and age only; local test on spring 2026 inquiries found disparities (section 7.4); full local test due 2026-12-15
monitoring: Weekly contact-within-48-hours rate by group; quarterly flag-rate ratios
state_admt_exposure_2027: Yes (Colorado and California applicants and inquiries)

use_case: Student-success risk scoring: weekly risk score for each enrolled student that sets advisor outreach lists
vendor_or_model: Company-built gradient-boosted model on the Cloud provider B machine learning platform (SYS-07)
data_categories: LMS activity (login counts, submissions); grades; credits; transfer credits; account holds; age; modality; program; four ISIR-derived fields (Pell eligibility, aid index band, dependency status, first-generation status; removal due 2026-11-30, POAM-004)
consequential_decision_category: None directly (routes supportive outreach); becomes Education if used for admission, aid, standing, or placement
human_in_the_loop: Advisor reviews each flagged student and decides whether and how to reach out; overrides recorded; no automated action on a student
applicable_laws: FERPA 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1) (legitimate educational interest; reasonable methods); HEA section 483 (FAFSA data limits); Title VI; Title IX; Section 504; Age Discrimination Act; California CPPA ADMT rules (counsel confirming exposure)
committee_review: Reviewed 2025-10-21; 2026-01 model refresh added ISIR-derived features without re-review; re-reviewed 2026-08-25
protected_characteristic_inputs: Age; ISIR-derived fields (proxies for income); LMS login counts (proxy for modality and work schedule)
bias_testing_status: Last full test on 2025 data; spring 2026 retest found 2 disparities (section 7.4); retest after retraining due 2027-01-31
monitoring: Session-end validity and fairness report; monthly 100-note advisor sample for prohibited uses

use_case: Online proctoring behavior flagging: flags possible misconduct in webcam-proctored exams for instructor review
vendor_or_model: Proctoring vendor AI feature (face detection, gaze and audio anomaly detection) in SYS-12
data_categories: Webcam video and audio; screen activity; exam metadata (education records)
human_in_the_loop: Proctoring staff review every flag before it reaches the instructor; flags alone cannot support a misconduct finding (academic integrity procedure); students can appeal
applicable_laws: FERPA (vendor as school official, 99.31(a)(1)(i)(B)); Section 504 and ADA (accommodations); state biometric privacy laws where students reside (counsel review); FTC Safeguards Rule 314.4(f) (vendor)
status: In production (about 410,000 proctored exams a year)
protected_characteristic_inputs: Face detection performance can vary with skin tone and lighting; disability-related movement
bias_testing_status: Local test 2026-01: face-not-detected rate differed by self-reported race (ratio 1.9); lighting guidance and human pre-review added; retest due 2027-01-31
monitoring: Quarterly flag rates and confirmed-misconduct rates by group and accommodation status
state_admt_exposure_2027: Yes (consequential education decision in Colorado from 2027-01-01)

use_case: Application fraud scoring that flags likely synthetic identities ("ghost students") in online applications for identity verification
vendor_or_model: CRM vendor fraud scoring rules and model, plus company rules
data_categories: Application data; device and network signals; email and phone reputation; document upload metadata
consequential_decision_category: Education (enrollment and Title IV aid can be held pending identity verification)
human_in_the_loop: Fraud analysts review every flag; a flagged applicant is asked to verify identity and is never denied on the score alone; OIG referral decisions are made by financial aid under written criteria
applicable_laws: Title IV fraud referral (34 CFR 668.16(g)); Title VI; Section 504; FERPA once matriculated; FTC Safeguards Rule 314.4(f)
status: In production (1.8% of 2026 online applications flagged)
protected_characteristic_inputs: Device and network signals can act as proxies for income and national origin
bias_testing_status: Local test 2026-06: flag-rate ratios within 0.8 to 1.25 for race and sex; age 50+ ratio 1.31 under review
monitoring: Monthly false positive rate (verified real applicants among flags) by group; OIG referral log
